questions: Can we reverse the direction of all edges multiple times, or is it a one-time operation?
After reversing edges, do we stay at the same vertex or move to a different vertex?
Is the reversal operation allowed at any time, including when no outgoing edge exists from the current vertex?
Do we need to consider that edges might become self-loops or duplicate edges after reversal?
Is the cost X incurred per reversal, regardless of how many edges are reversed?
Can we move along an edge and then immediately reverse edges in the same step, or are operations discrete?
Are we allowed to reverse edges even if it doesn't help reach vertex N, just incurring cost?
Does the guarantee that we can reach vertex N apply to the initial graph only, or also after any number of reversals?
